items.title: Two CultureMech recipes are both named gyps_medium — the GYPS link's uniqueness was never checkable
items.body:
Surfaced by the hardened matcher in #489, running against the real recipe tree. Not a defect in that PR — the link is correct — but a live ambiguity the old tooling structurally could not show.

## Two recipes, one name

```
CultureMech:002799  data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/gyps_medium.yaml
  original_name: GYPS MEDIUM
  Glucose, Yeast extract, Peptone, Sea Salt, MES

CultureMech:009837  data/normalized_yaml/bacterial/TOGO_M450_GYPS_Medium.yaml
  original_name: GYPS Medium
  Distilled water, Yeast extract, MES, Sea salts (Sigma), Glucose, Peptone, N2
```

Same core formulation from two sources; 009837 additionally lists water and an N2 atmosphere.

## Why this matters

MIM's `GYPS` record links to **CultureMech:002799**, and that choice is defensible — its evidence reads *"CultureMech additionally lists MES and Sea Salt and no starch"*, which describes 002799's five ingredients exactly. So the verification was done against that record and the link is right.

**But its uniqueness was never checked, and could not have been.** The old matcher indexed recipes in a one-value dict keyed on lower-cased name, so only one of the two `gyps_medium` recipes was ever visible; the curator saw whichever happened to be indexed last. That the surviving one was the correct one is luck, not process.

Now that the index is multi-valued, `GYPS` reports as ambiguous with both ids, which is the honest state.

## What to decide

Is `CultureMech:009837` a **duplicate** of 002799 (a CultureMech-side dedup, in #218/#219's neighbourhood) or a **distinct variant** worth its own record? If the latter, MIM's `GYPS` may warrant a second reference — the schema added in #489 supports `VARIANT_OF` for exactly this.

No change to the existing link is proposed here: `culturemech_reference.medium_id` already names 002799 unambiguously, which is the whole point of carrying an id rather than a name.

## Scale

This is one instance of a general condition: **2291 CultureMech names are shared by more than one recipe**, and `defined_freshwater_medium_cocl2` names 29. Any future link verified by name has the same exposure; the ambiguity flag in `reports/culturemech_link_candidates.tsv` is what makes it visible.

items.title: IngredientTypeEnum mixes two axes: BHI is a named medium AND compositionally undefined, and the schema cannot say both

labels.name: needs-human
labels.description: Hard stop for agents. Ontology minting, deletions, schema changes.

items.body:
Split out from #222, which asks whether to rename `DEFINED_MEDIUM`. Renaming fixes the misleading label; it does not fix this.

## The conflation

`IngredientTypeEnum` has four permissible values. Three describe **record granularity**:

- `SINGLE_INGREDIENT` — one compound
- `DEFINED_MEDIUM` — a whole named medium
- `STOCK_SOLUTION` — a premixed solution

One describes **composition**:

- `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE` — "complex mixture of unknown or variable composition"

These are orthogonal properties sharing one slot, so a record that is both must discard one.

## The live case

`BHI` (brain heart infusion) is a complete, named medium — and it is compositionally undefined, being built from infusions. It is one of only two records carrying `culturemech_medium_name`, i.e. it is explicitly linked to a CultureMech *recipe*.

It is classified `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE`, and its own curator note says why:

> state no composition to split on. ingredient_type=UNDEFINED_MIXTURE

The curator picked the composition axis. #216's clarification says the enum encodes granularity. Both readings are defensible because the enum genuinely holds both, and nothing can flag the disagreement — the record is internally consistent and passes validation either way.

The cost is that `DEFINED_MEDIUM`'s 127 records and `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE`'s 138 are not a partition of anything. You cannot ask "which records are whole media?" and get an answer, because an unknown number of whole media are filed under the other value.

## CultureMech already models this correctly

Every normalized recipe carries both axes as separate fields:

```yaml
id: CultureMech:008339
name: tyl_medium
medium_type: COMPLEX
composition_type: UNDEFINED
```

So the sibling repo can express "a named medium of undefined composition" and MIM cannot, for the same substances.

## Proposal

Give composition its own field, mirroring CultureMech's vocabulary, and leave `IngredientTypeEnum` as a clean granularity axis:

- `IngredientTypeEnum`: `SINGLE_INGREDIENT` / `NAMED_MEDIUM` (per #222) / `STOCK_SOLUTION`
- new `composition_type`: `DEFINED` / `UNDEFINED` / `PARTIALLY_DEFINED`

Migration is mechanical for the unambiguous cases — every current `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE` becomes `composition_type: UNDEFINED` plus a granularity value. The granularity value is the judgement call, and BHI shows it is a real one: the 138 `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE` records need review to say which are whole media and which are single complex components (yeast extract, peptone). That review is the actual work here, and it is worth doing because it is currently unanswerable from the data.

## Sequencing

Do **#222's rename first** — it is cheap, unblocked, and strictly an improvement. This issue is the larger follow-up and should not hold it up. Note that if both land, the 127 records get touched twice; if that matters, do them in one migration, but do not let this issue's review burden delay the rename.

## Not in scope

Reinterpreting CultureMech recipe variants or families, which is CultureMech#339's neighbourhood.

items.title: Validate SSSOM object_match_field against curated synonyms
items.body:
## Problem

The published `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv` stores curated aliases in `object_match_field`, but `scripts/reconcile_sssom.py` only validates row presence, orphan/stale ontology IDs, and ontology-row predicates.

That leaves final SSSOM able to carry stale synonym text after a curated record's synonym list changes.

## Evidence

While fixing #137, `Proteose peptone no. 2` was split from the generic `Proteose Peptone` record into `kgmicrobe.ingredient:proteose_peptone_no_2` with a `skos:narrowMatch` to `MICRO:0000180`.

The generic `MIM:Proteose_Peptone` SSSOM exact-match row still published these stale aliases in `object_match_field` until the row was manually edited:

- `Proteose peptone no. 2`
- `Proteose peptone No 2 (DIFCO 0121-01-3)`

## Scope

Add a currency check for `object_match_field` on SSSOM rows whose subject still exists and whose current ontology row is not stale.

items.title: SSSOM review: prevent implicit exact-match upgrades and invalid source ownership
items.body:
The supported SSSOM review must not inherit an exact relation when the original review only supports a close parent or when catalog aliases collapse distinct formulations.

Pre-finalization full SSSOM SHA256: `aa328df9bab3d7a5cf555c0200d43c6987820268f2b48757d8d203b281d3f809` (3,018 rows). Four rows currently have inherited APPROVED decisions that exceed their evidence:

| Source position | Exact row | Evidence conflict |
| --- | --- | --- |
| 1323 | `MIM:Glucose_1-phosphate skos:exactMatch CHEBI:16077` | YAML and its positive report explicitly support CLOSE_MATCH because source stereochemistry is unspecified. |
| 1518 | `MIM:Isocitrate skos:exactMatch CHEBI:16087` | YAML and its positive report preserve CLOSE_MATCH to a charge-specific species under an assumed pH. |
| 2658 | `MIM:Soy_Peptone skos:exactMatch FOODON:03315720` | Source and report explicitly describe a close parent, hydrolyzed vegetable protein, not an exact soy-peptone term. |
| 2153 | `MIM:Nutrient_Broth_No_2 skos:exactMatch MICRO:0000082` | The approved `other` field treats Nutrient Broth No.2 and BD 234000 as catalog aliases even though primary recipes differ. |

For Nutrient Broth No.2, [NITE NBRC medium 1559](https://www.nite.go.jp/nbrc/catalogue/NBRCMediumDetailServlet?NO=1559) identifies Oxoid CM0067B with 10 g/L Lab-Lemco, 10 g/L peptone and 5 g/L NaCl. [ATCC medium 3](https://www.atcc.org/-/media/product-assets/documents/microbial-media-formulations/3/atcc-medium-3.pdf?rev=7510837507e64d849c62a46b5b2197a1) identifies BD 234000 at 8 g/L, with the scratch formula 3 g/L beef extract and 5 g/L peptone. [The manufacturer](https://www.thermofisher.com/order/catalog/product/CM0067B) also distinguishes No.2 from standard Oxoid Nutrient Broth CM0001. These formulations cannot be certified as one catalog identity simply by removing the No.2 qualifier.

The original report paths are `reports/yaml_record_review/{Glucose_1-phosphate,Isocitrate,Soy_Peptone,Nutrient_Broth_No_2}.md`. Machine findings include exact assertion hashes, row payloads, report hashes/excerpts and primary-source summaries in the review evidence ledger.

Resolution for the present supported-only release:

- Bind explicit WITHHOLD dispositions to all four final row payloads, preserve their full claims and reasons in the separate backlog, and exclude them from the supported SSSOM.
- Reject inherited ontology `skos:exactMatch` approval when source mapping quality is CLOSE_MATCH, NARROW_MATCH, BROAD_MATCH, PLACEHOLDER or LEXICAL_MATCH unless an explicit row-specific review supports the exact relation and complete alias surface. A self-identifier equality rule is not scientific evidence. Registry rows require their own scoped review.
- Keep the Nutrient Broth No.2 hold explicit even though its source grade is EXACT_MATCH; this case survives the grade guard.
- Verify that rebuilding cannot silently reapprove these rows and that final row hashes/dispositions cover every complete SSSOM row. Future corrections can recover source-specific identities without inventing a formula or replacement target in this publication repair.

This closes the release-approval defect by withholding unsupported claims; it does not claim that the four source identity problems have all been scientifically corrected.

## Export ownership bypass

The new standalone exporter initially accepted a nonexistent MIM subject when its label matched an existing record, and accepted an incorrect label when the subject matched. All 3,018 current subjects have canonical filename CURIE matches, so no fallback is required. Require both subject and exact preferred label to identify the same MAPPED source record. Add adversarial tests for unknown/mismatched subjects and labels and non-MAPPED owners.

## Further adversarial findings addressed in this branch

- The previously supported 1,2-dichloropropane and calcium chloride dihydrate rows contain concentration-qualified preparations as pure-compound synonyms; sodium nitrate includes an autoclaving instruction; SPIR solution aliases numbered formulations without composition evidence. Preserve these four current rows in the withheld backlog.
- Resolving #724 initially preserved the original negative review fields but did not validate the historical assertion payload against its digest. A rewritten historical payload could pass. Verify the original payload hash and retain its frozen decision.
- The graph gate initially checked mapping decision positions without requiring the standalone review to describe the identical canonical SSSOM source and payloads. Require canonical path/hash and complete ordered row equality.
- Evidence was initially hashed and parsed in separate reads, allowing a file mutation between those operations to substitute a positive proof. Parse the exact verified bytes and recheck the complete input snapshot.
- Partial output writes could corrupt an existing export. Stage and validate a complete generation before publication, with rollback on failure.
- A supported asymmetric mapping could lack its required supported registry identity sibling. Validate that subset invariant without automatically promoting an unreviewed sibling.
- Native SSSOM parsing can log and drop an invalid row before schema validation, which then accepts the empty result. Assert raw/native/manifest row-count equality and the complete identity/label/confidence multiset with duplicate multiplicity; validate numeric confidence rather than treating a quiet parser as proof of completeness.
- Explicit changed-owner decisions must remain bound to the reviewed row and owner hashes. Freeze the input inventory and verify those fields before adoption.

These release and integrity defects are resolved by precise withholding, source correction, and regression checks. Source research still needed to rehabilitate withheld claims remains in #718 and the separate mapping backlog; closing this issue does not declare those source claims scientifically corrected.

## Final integration review

The current-semantic-review link presented prior-release counts and receipts alongside updated ledgers, overstating currency. Mark the prior graph release as historical and point current mapping consumers to the completed standalone SSSOM review.

The synonym-correction batch also crossed the unified table's accumulated record-drift budget. Regenerate the table using the previously reviewed isolated-input wrapper, retain all explicit rejected-ID protections, record the input/output hashes, and stamp freshness only after a successful rebuild and rejection check.

items.title: Stale chebi_id/culturemech_term_id columns outrank corrected kg_microbe_node_id/mim_id (3 superseded groundings re-asserted)
items.body:
While implementing a retraction pass in kg-microbe for the 16 superseded groundings flagged in `culturebotai-claw` `workspace/reports/propagation_2026-07-19.md`, we found that **3 of the 16 are not just re-seeding phantoms** — kg-microbe's `load_culturebotai_reviewed` **actively re-asserts them every run** from the current `UNIFIED_INGREDIENT_MAPPING.tsv`, because a corrected grounding was written to `kg_microbe_node_id` / `mim_id` while the **superseded value was left in a higher-precedence column** (`chebi_id` / `culturemech_term_id`).

## Mechanism

The kg-microbe loader selects the primary CURIE with:

```
best_primary([chebi_id, culturemech_term_id, mim_id, kg_microbe_node_id, cas_rn])
```

Within one prefix (e.g. all `CHEBI:`) the rank is equal, so the **first candidate in that list wins** — `chebi_id` outranks `kg_microbe_node_id` / `mim_id`. When a correction updates `kg_microbe_node_id` / `mim_id` but leaves the old id in `chebi_id` (or `culturemech_term_id`), the consumer grounds to the **stale** value and demotes the correction to a mere xref.

## The 3 cases (current file)

| ingredient(s) | consumer picks (stale) | intended (in kg_node/mim) | stale column(s) |
|---|---|---|---|
| 4-Aminobenzoic acid, PABA, Para-aminobenzoic acid | `CHEBI:194474` (4-ammoniobenzoate) | `CHEBI:30753` (4-aminobenzoic acid) | `chebi_id`, `culturemech_term_id` |
| Cobalamine | `CHEBI:30411` (cobalamin) | `CHEBI:28911` (Cobalamine) | `chebi_id`, `culturemech_term_id` |
| Infusion from Potatoes | `FOODON:03316428` (**Peptone**) | — (Peptone is wrong for a potato infusion) | `culturemech_term_id` |

Notes:
- For the PABA *variant* rows (`p-Amino Benzoic Acid`, `p-amino benzoic acid`; status `CHEBI_NO_MIM`), `kg_microbe_node_id` / `mim_id` are **empty** and only `chebi_id` / `culturemech_term_id = CHEBI:194474` are set — so those rows assert *only* the stale id. The correction (`CHEBI:30753`) exists only on the canonical `4-Aminobenzoic acid` row.
- The ~80 peptone/tryptone/casein rows also historically grounded to `FOODON:03316428` are **already fixed** (`MICRO:0000178` peptone, `MICRO:0000182` tryptone, `MICRO:0000180` proteose peptone, `FOODON:03315719` casein hydrolysate, …). `FOODON:03316428` ("Peptone") now survives only through the single mis-annotated "Infusion from Potatoes" row.

## Suggested fix

When a grounding is corrected, also **clear or update the superseded value in `chebi_id` and `culturemech_term_id`** (and propagate the correction to all name-variant rows), so each row has a single consistent source of truth. Otherwise the stale column silently outranks the correction in any consumer that ranks id columns by position. For "Infusion from Potatoes", the `culturemech_term_id = FOODON:03316428` ("Peptone") looks like a mis-annotation to fix or drop.

## kg-microbe side (context, no action needed here)

kg-microbe now runs a retraction pass that drops these every consolidation, and the correct groundings are independently present, so the published graph is clean. We deliberately did **not** reorder the consumer's column precedence (`kg_microbe_node_id`-first), because that would shift ~35 unrelated groundings (Fructose, Cholesterol, Casein, …) that need separate curation review. This issue is only so the root cause is fixed in the source data.

_Reported from KG-Microbe consolidation tooling._

items.title: 30 ontology CURIEs are held by two or more LIVE records, which MIM's own rule forbids
items.body:
Found while fixing #407. That issue is a rendering defect; this is the data defect underneath it, and it is the more serious of the two.

In MIM a mapped record's `identifier` **is** its ontology CURIE. Two live records on the same CURIE therefore assert that two different ingredients are the same thing — the `Butane-1,4-diol` lesson, generalised.

Counting identifiers held by more than one record in the curated collections:

| shape | count | verdict |
|---|---:|---|
| MAPPED + REJECTED | 47 | **correct** — the merge-tombstone pattern; a tombstone deliberately carries the winner's identifier |
| **MAPPED + MAPPED** | **30** | **defect** |

The 30 split into two quite different problems, and they need opposite fixes.

**Genuine duplicates that should be merged:**

```
MICRO:0000182   'Bacto-tryptone' / 'Tryptone' (6 occ) / 'Tryptone peptone'
MICRO:0000178   'Bacto peptone' / 'Peptone'
MICRO:0000193   'Bacto brain heart infusion' / 'Brain heart infusion' / 'Brain heart infusion broth'
CHEBI:3312      'CaCl2' (502 occ) / 'Calcium Chloride' (15 occ)
CHEBI:86158     'CaCl22H2O' (2) / 'CaCl2 x 2 H2O' (4,343)
ENVO:00002263   'Garden soil' / 'air-dried garden soil'
```

These are notation or branding variants of one substance. Standard merge: keep the higher-occurrence label, fold the other in as a `RAW_TEXT` synonym.

**Distinct substances wrongly sharing one identifier** — these must NOT be merged:

```
CHEBI:31346     'CaSO4' (9)          vs 'CaSO4 x 7 H2O' (2)
CHEBI:30769     'Citric acid' (63)   vs 'Citric Acid•H2O' (3)
FOODON:03315719 'Casein peptone'     vs 'Casamino acids' (395)
MICRO:0000455   'Algal Trace Elements Solution' vs 'WC Trace Elements Solution'
```

An anhydrous salt and its heptahydrate have different CAS numbers, different formula weights and are ordered separately — `MAPPING_SEMANTICS` §"map to what you can order" is explicit that the orderability rule does **not** license collapsing them. One of each pair needs re-grounding to its own term, or a `kgmicrobe.compound:` mint where no term exists.

## Why nothing caught it

`validate_sssom_invariants.py` checks Rules A/B1/B2/B3/C over the SSSOM, none of which constrain identifier uniqueness among live records. The visualisation gate added in #405 checks that every published node names a record that exists — the converse. So an identifier can be issued twice and every gate stays green.

Worth a uniqueness gate once the 30 are triaged: live records must hold distinct identifiers, with tombstones explicitly exempt. Filing the count now so it cannot grow unnoticed while the triage waits.

items.title: Two mapped records share MICRO:0000178, and glycogen is mapped twice (CHEBI:28087 and cas:9005-79-2)
items.body:
Found reviewing #214, which had to work around it.

`data/curated/mapped_ingredients.yaml` holds more than one MAPPED record for the same identifier:

| identifier | records |
|---|---|
| `MICRO:0000178` | `preferred_term: Bacto peptone` **and** `preferred_term: Peptone` |

and the same ingredient under two different identifier schemes:

| ingredient | records |
|---|---|
| glycogen | `CHEBI:28087` (`Glycogen`) **and** `cas:9005-79-2` |

In MIM the record `identifier` **is** the ontology mapping CURIE, so two records with one CURIE are two records claiming to be the same term. The CHEBI/cas pair is the dual-identifier case `review-ingredients` is meant to catch.

## Why it bites

Any tool that indexes records by identifier — the obvious `{r['identifier']: r for r in ...}` — silently keeps whichever record comes last. #214 merges raw labels into existing mapped records, so a last-wins lookup would have attached `Peptones` and `Peptone (0.01 %` to whichever peptone record happened to sort last, with a `curation_history` entry asserting the merge was deliberate. It now resolves targets by CURIE **and** `preferred_term` and raises on ambiguity, but that is a guard around the defect, not a fix.

`reconcile_sssom.py` keys SSSOM subjects off `preferred_term` of MAPPED records, so a duplicated CURIE also means two SSSOM subjects pointing at one object.

## Suggested fix

Merge each pair with the `merge-ingredients` procedure — keep the ontology-backed record (`CHEBI:28087`, and one of the two peptone records), fold the other's synonyms and occurrence statistics in, tombstone the loser. Then add a `qc` assertion that no identifier appears twice across the mapped collection; that invariant is cheap and nothing currently checks it.

items.title: 106 SSSOM rows publish another record's preferred_term as their own synonym
items.body:
Measured while scoping #622.

`other` is merged into the ontology entity's synonym set by kg-microbe, so a token there is a name the subject answers to. **115 tokens across 106 rows are the preferred_term of a *different* MIM record.**

```
MIM:2-Deoxyadenosine_Monohydrate                      '2-deoxyadenosine'
MIM:A-Ketoglutaric_Acid_Disodium_Salt_Hydrate         'alpha-ketoglutaric acid'
MIM:2-Keto-D-gluconic_Acid_Hemicalcium_Salt_Hydrate   '2-Keto-D-gluconic acid hemicalcium salt monohydrate'
MIM:84_GL_NaHCO3_Solution                             'NaHCO3'
MIM:4-Methyl-2-oxopentanoic_Acid_Sodium_Salt          '4-Methyl-2-oxovaleric acid'
MIM:24-diamino-67-di-iso-propylpteridine_phosphate    'Vibriostat'
```

Each right-hand name is a record in its own right. So the monohydrate claims the anhydrous compound's name, the disodium salt hydrate claims the free acid's name, and a prepared solution claims the pure compound's name — which is exactly the hydrate/anhydrous and salt/free-acid conflation MAPPING_SEMANTICS §3 exists to prevent, arriving through the synonym channel instead of through `identifier`.

It is #232's defect ("one published label resolves to more than one identifier") in the column nobody checks. Rule H pins it for `subject_label`; nothing pins it for `other`.

## Where it comes from

`other` is assembled in claw as

```python
candidate_alts = [mim_stored_label] + [kgm_name] + kgm_syns + mim_yaml_syns
```

so most of its content is **kg-microbe's synonyms for the ontology term**, not MIM's. When two MIM records share one CHEBI parent — which is the norm for a hydrate family — the parent's synonym list is merged into *each* of them, and each ends up claiming its siblings' names.

That also means MIM cannot validate `other` currency in general (it does not own most of the content), which is the correction #622 needs: the decidable, MIM-side property is not "are these synonyms current" but **"no record's `other` may contain another record's preferred_term"**.

## Verified clean alongside it

`other` republishing a token the same record marks `REJECTED_LABEL`: **0**. The builder's `NON_PUBLISHABLE_MIM_SYNONYM_TYPES` filter is holding.

## Suggested disposition

Add the cross-record check as an SSSOM invariant with a baseline of the 115 known violations, so new ones are blocked while the existing set is triaged — the pattern `mappings/duplicate_identifier_baseline.tsv` already uses here. Clearing the baseline means a claw rebuild, since `other` is generated there.

| 95 | `FOODON:03315719` / `mesh:C017721` (Casamino acids) |
| 34 | `MICRO:0000460` + 5 `kgmicrobe.ingredient:*` vitamin solutions |
| 28 | `FOODON:03315719` / `MICRO:0000182` (Pancreatic digest of casein) |
| 19 | `CHEBI:17439` / `CHEBI:176843` (Vitamin B12) |
| 14 | `CHEBI:3312` / `CHEBI:86158` (CaCl2 2H2O) |
| 14 | `CHEBI:91247` / `kgmicrobe.ingredient:l-cysteine_x_hcl_x_h2o_solution` |
| 10 | `CHEBI:31795` / `CHEBI:32599` (MgSO4 7H2O) |
| 5 | `CHEBI:35696` / `kgmicrobe.compound:cocl2_x_2_h2o` / `cocl2_x_4_h2o` |
| 3 | `CHEBI:17909` / `CHEBI:26833` (sulfur) |

These are not all one defect. At least three kinds are mixed here, and they want different
answers:

1. **Duplicate records on one substance** — `Sea Salt`, `Casamino acids`. A merge under the
   `merge-ingredients` skill.
2. **Granularity disagreement** — `CHEBI:17909` (sulfur atom) vs `CHEBI:26833` (elemental
   sulfur); `CHEBI:17439` (cyanocobalamin) vs `CHEBI:176843` (cobalamin). A decision under
   MAPPING_SEMANTICS Section 3, not a merge.
3. **A wrong synonym on a hydrate sibling, which is an identity error rather than an
   ambiguity.** `CoCl2 6H2O` matches records for the **di**- and **tetra**-hydrate, so
   those records carry a hexahydrate spelling they do not denote. Same shape for
   `CaCl2 2H2O` against `CHEBI:3312`, which is anhydrous calcium chloride. Hydration state
   is identity (MAPPING_SEMANTICS Section 3): these synonyms should be removed regardless
   of how the ambiguity is resolved.

Kind 3 is the one worth doing first -- it is a wrong claim now being published, whereas
kinds 1 and 2 are unresolved questions.

Not addressed in the grounding PR that found this: resolving these needs per-family
judgement, and the PR deliberately skips every shared identifier rather than picking an
owner arbitrarily.

items.title: 17 records carry the same synonym twice, inflating the label index and the other cap
items.body:
Found in adversarial review of #528 (pre-existing; that PR neither caused nor worsened it).

17 records carry the same synonym text twice, compared casefolded:

```
Distilled_Water.yaml            'sterile dh2o'
Alk_So42.yaml                   'aluminum potassium sulfate'
Na2glycerophosphate5h2o.yaml    'na2glycerophosphate•5h2o(cas: 13408-09-8)'
Casein_Peptone.yaml             'casein hydrolysate', 'casein enzymic hydrolysate'
```

Count is identical on `origin/main`, so this predates the surface-form work. The
backfill's own duplicate check kept it from growing.

Low severity, but not nothing:

* `export_lists.py` emits one `label_index.csv` row per synonym, so a duplicate
  synonym produces two identical index rows for the same record. The lookup still
  resolves, but the index is larger than the corpus it describes and row counts stop
  being a usable measure of coverage — which is the number this work has been tracking
  throughout.
* The builder pipes synonyms into SSSOM `other`, where `_pipe` caps at
  `MAX_OTHER_ENTRIES = 50`. On a crowded row a duplicate consumes a slot that a distinct
  surface form would otherwise get, and the cap is documented as biting hardest on the
  hydrate families.

The fix is a de-duplicating pass over `synonyms`, casefolded, keeping the first
occurrence and preferring the more specific `synonym_type` when the duplicates disagree
(e.g. a `RAW_TEXT` and an `EXACT_SYNONYM` of the same string). Worth pairing with a guard
so it cannot recur, since several writers append synonyms and only some check first.

items.title: CHEBI grounding pass — results, curation report & open follow-ups
items.body:
A CHEBI-grounding pass over MIM's ungrounded ingredients (CAS→CHEBI via the local ChEBI dbxref index, complex-ingredient resolver, non-chemical flagging), relying on MIM's curated data + kg-microbe. **Finding: MIM is already well-curated** — of ~2,206 ungrounded unified rows, the substantive results were a handful of corrections, not a mass grounding.

## Landed (reviewed clean by Fable 5)
- **PR #112** — CHEBI grounding + curation:
  - Gepotidacin `cas:1075236-89-3` → `CHEBI:747127` (skos:exactMatch; unique CAS dbxref + label-exact).
  - Glycogen from bovine liver: `cas:` FALLBACK → `CHEBI:28087` (glycogen), exactMatch (source qualifier).
  - Beef extract: removed erroneous `cas_rn 103-47-9` (that CAS is CHES / `CHEBI:44302` — a PubChem name-lookup false positive); stays on `FOODON:03302088`.
  - SSSOM reconciled in-sync; invariants A/B1/B2/B3 pass.
- **PR #113** — periodic `UNIFIED_INGREDIENT_MAPPING.tsv` refresh (3,853→3,937 rows, CHEBI 1,647→1,668). Reviewer confirmed 100% CHEBI internal consistency.

## Already-correct (curation queue items that needed no change)
- sn-glycerol-3-phosphate lithium salt → `CHEBI:15978` (NARROW_MATCH, matches sibling salts).
- carnitine-DL-HCl → `CHEBI:17126` (carnitine, stereo-unspecified parent — correct for a DL racemate).

## Open follow-ups
- [ ] **Audit PubChem-sourced `cas_rn` for other false-positives.** Beef extract's `103-47-9` (=CHES) was a name-lookup mis-assignment by `fetch_cas_rn_from_pubchem`. Cross-check `chemical_properties.cas_rn` (esp. on `UNDEFINED_MIXTURE`/complex records) against CHEBI/expected formula to catch other bad CAS.
- [ ] **45 flagged non-chemicals** need disposition (not CHEBI-groundable): ~10 placeholders ("See source for composition"), ~20 complex mixtures/solutions, ~7 environmental/media, ~8 buffers (borderline). Decide: leave UNMAPPED, map to FOODON/ENVO, or mark NON_CHEMICAL.
- [ ] **Complex-resolver NO_HIT peptones** (Peptone, Proteose peptone, Trypticase peptone, …) would map cleanly to **MICRO** (`MICRO:0000178` = peptone) — deferred; needs the `MICRO:` prefix added to the SSSOM curie_map + builder.
- [ ] **Possible pre-existing mis-mapping:** `Carnitine Hydrochloride` → `CHEBI:48601` "carnitinamide chloride" — carnitinamide is the amide (a different compound); a curator should confirm vs carnitine/carnitinium chloride.

Full pipeline report (per-tier counts, all candidates) is captured in PR #112's description. Spec + report live in the session scratchpad (`GROUNDING_SPEC.md`, `chebi_grounding_report.md`).

items.title: Re-ground 3 SSSOM rows to MICRO ids with malformed upstream IRIs
items.body:
Follow-up from #119, found by the new CURIE normalizer (`just curie-verify-micro`).

MicrO mints ~1,472 of its 3,450 classes under a malformed IRI —
`http://purl.obolibrary.org/obo/MicrO.owl/MICRO_nnnnnnn` instead of
`.../obo/MICRO_nnnnnnn`. OLS4 reports `is_defining_ontology: false` for those and
the canonical PURL 404s, so the CURIE does not round-trip.

**Three such ids are already published in `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv`:**

| CURIE | label | 
|---|---|
| `MICRO:0002250` | V-8 juice |
| `MICRO:0002392` | rabbit serum |
| `MICRO:0002393` | Proteose Peptone No. 2 |

The other 31 MICRO ids in the SSSOM verify clean.

These need either a re-grounding to a well-formed term, or an upstream fix in
MicrO. Until then they are excluded from `test_every_published_object_id_normalises`
via `KNOWN_BAD_MICRO` in `tests/test_curie_normalizer.py`; a companion test
asserts the exclusion does not outlive the defect.

Detection: `just curie-verify-micro`. Context: `docs/CURIE_STANDARD.md` §3.

Note for triage — do **not** use PURL status to judge these. Term-level PURLs 404
for *all* of MicrO, well-formed or not (control PURLs for CHEBI/FOODON/UBERON
return 200). Use `is_defining_ontology` and the IRI shape.

items.title: Consider renaming IngredientTypeEnum.DEFINED_MEDIUM (cross-Mech) — description clarified in #216
items.body:
Follow-up to #168 (closed by #216).

#216 took the low-risk path: it sharpened the `DEFINED_MEDIUM` description to say the value denotes **record granularity** (a complete named medium), not the microbiology term of art "chemically defined medium". That removes the immediate docs hazard but leaves the **enum name** itself still reading as "chemically defined" to anyone who doesn't open the description.

The honest fix is a rename (e.g. `NAMED_MEDIUM` / `COMPLETE_MEDIUM` / `MEDIUM_FORMULATION`), but it is **cross-Mech**:
- CultureMech imports MIM's enums, so the token must change in lockstep (coordinate via culturebotai-claw / the vendored-schema path `mech_shared.yaml` if the enum lives there, or a synchronized rename if it is MIM-owned).
- 53 MIM records currently carry `DEFINED_MEDIUM`, and kg-microbe consumes the value — a rename needs a data migration + a consumer heads-up.

Decision needed: is the description-only clarification sufficient long-term, or do we schedule the coordinated rename? Not blocking; parked so it is not lost when #168 closes.

items.title: Four verified wrong CHEBI groundings the no-op plausibility gate was hiding
items.body:
Surfaced by pointing the plausibility gate at the curator label (#261). These are **not** naming-convention noise — each is a record asserting a CHEBI id for an unrelated molecule, verified against live `sqlite:obo:chebi`.

| record | asserted id | what the id actually is | what the ingredient is |
|---|---|---|---|
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Casamino_Acids.yaml` | CHEBI:78020 | **heptacosanoate** (C27 fatty acid anion) | acid-hydrolysed casein digest — a peptide/amino-acid mixture |
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Na2s2o4.yaml` | CHEBI:61278 | **scutellarin** (a flavone glucuronide) | sodium dithionite, Na₂S₂O₄ — a reducing agent |
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Sodium_Succinate_Dibasic.yaml` | CHEBI:150903 | a trisaccharide-type glycoside (`(2S,3S,4R,5S,6S)-2-[…]oxane-3,4,5-triol`) | disodium succinate |
| `data/ingredients/mapped/Tomatidine_Hydrochloride.yaml` | CHEBI:93130 | `1-methyl-3-[…]-1,3,5-triazinane-2,4,6-trione` | tomatidine HCl, a steroidal alkaloid |

`Casamino acids → heptacosanoate` and `Na2S2O4 → scutellarin` are the starkest: nothing about either pair is chemically close, and both are common media ingredients, so the wrong id propagates into every export and downstream KG edge.

## Also worth a look (different failure class)

`Fructooligosaccharides (FOS)` → CHEBI:28645 **beta-D-fructofuranose**. Not an unrelated molecule, but a **granularity** error: a single monosaccharide standing in for an oligosaccharide mixture. Closer to the #237/#216 `DEFINED_MEDIUM` discussion than to the four above.

## Scope note

The gate reported 61 `IMPLAUSIBLE_LABEL` in total. **Most of the rest look like correct groundings** the lexical heuristic cannot see — `2-Furfuraldehyde` → *furfural*, `Irgasan` → *triclosan*, `Sodium 2-mercaptoethanesulfonate` → *Mesna*, `Soy peptone` → *vegetable protein, hydrolyzed* (the very example the validator's own comment cites as a legitimate no-shared-word case). So the 61 is a **triage queue, not a defect count**, which is exactly why #261 holds this surface at `severity: warn` rather than flipping it to `error`.

These four, though, are confirmed and should be re-grounded.

Related: #261, #114.

items.title: Pre-existing collection<->per-record drift (stale mapped/ files, duplicate-state records)
items.body:
Surfaced while curating PR #145. Not caused by that work; filing so it is not lost.

## What
The curated collections (`data/curated/{mapped,unmapped}_ingredients.yaml`) and the per-record corpus (`data/ingredients/{mapped,unmapped}/*.yaml`) have drifted apart on `main` in several ways:

1. **Stale per-record files never re-exported.** Running `just export-individual` regenerates ~59 per-record files with content the collection already had (corrected mappings, curation notes) that the committed per-record files lack. The per-record files lag the collection.

2. **Duplicate-state records.** At least 3 records — `Phytone` (UNMAPPED_0488), `Soya_Pepton` (UNMAPPED_0531), `Tryptone_Peptone` (UNMAPPED_0558) — are listed as **UNMAPPED** in the collection but have a **mapped/** per-record file on disk. Re-exporting creates an `unmapped/` file for each while the stale `mapped/` file persists → the same identifier exists in two states/dirs.

## Why it matters
`aggregate-collections` (per-record -> collection) and `export-individual` (collection -> per-record) are supposed to be inverses, but the corpus and collection disagree, so a round-trip is not idempotent. The duplicate-state records are the worst case — a consumer reading the per-record tree sees a different mapping_status than one reading the collection.

## Suggested fix
A dedicated resync pass: pick the collection as canonical, run `export-individual`, delete orphaned stale per-record files, verify with `reconcile_sssom` + `validate-strict`, commit as its own reviewable PR. Do this **after** the filename-casing footgun #147 is fixed, since `export-individual` is the tool involved and would otherwise bake in the casing drift.

items.title: Merging a raw label into an existing record removes it from every flat export and from SSSOM
items.body:
Found reviewing #227. Applies to #214's 9 merges as well, and the new `merge_unmapped_into_mapped.py` guarantees it repeats.

## The regression

A merge deletes the UNMAPPED record and adds its raw label as a `RAW_TEXT` synonym on the target. By design it adds **no SSSOM row** — SSSOM subjects are `preferred_term`s of MAPPED records, never synonyms (`reconcile_sssom.py:74-82`), so adding one would be reported ORPHAN.

But `docs/data/{all,mapped,unmapped}_ingredients.csv` have **no synonyms column**:

    identifier,ontology_id,preferred_term,mapping_status,ontology_label,ontology_source,mapping_quality,total_occurrences,media_count

So after a merge the raw label appears in **no flat artifact at all**. Only `docs/data/ingredients.json` (which has `synonyms`/`searchable`) and the YAML retain it.

## Failure scenario

A kg-microbe consumer joining raw ingredient strings against `docs/data/all_ingredients.csv` or `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv`:

- **before** #227: `D-lactate` → `UNMAPPED_0654` — resolves to "known ingredient, not yet grounded"
- **after**: `D-lactate` → **nothing**

Record-level coverage went *up* (the label is now grounded to CHEBI:16004) while flat-surface coverage went *down*. That is the opposite of the intended effect, and it is invisible to every current gate: reconcile is GAP/ORPHAN/STALE 0, roundtrip is clean, qc-duplicate-ids is clean.

Affected so far: 5 labels from #227 (`3-hydroxy 2-butanone`, `D-lactate`, `Iso-butanol`, `N-acetyl-neuraminic Acid`, `Trimethyleneglycol`) and 9 from #214 (`2-dichloropropane`, `1% Sodium Chloride`, `Peptones`, …).

## Options

1. **Add a synonyms column to `export_lists.py`** — smallest change, keeps SSSOM semantics intact, makes the CSVs self-sufficient for string resolution.
2. **Emit a synonym-subject SSSOM row** with a distinct predicate — richer, but needs `reconcile_sssom.py` and the invariant validator taught about non-preferred_term subjects, and a decision on the right predicate.
3. Accept it and document that raw-string resolution must go through `ingredients.json`.

Option 1 looks right. Whichever is chosen, a check that every `RAW_TEXT` synonym is resolvable from at least one published flat artifact would stop this recurring.

Related: #227, #214, #220.

items.title: REJECTED and PENDING_REVIEW records sit in data/ingredients/mapped/ — 29 of them now
items.body:
Surfaced by #167, which made the collection headers honest: `data/curated/mapped_ingredients.yaml` now reports **1877 MAPPED + 2 non-MAPPED** against `total_count: 1879`. Previously the header claimed `mapped_count: 1877 / unmapped_count: 0` against 1879 records — self-inconsistent, so the 2 were invisible.

The 2 are `data/ingredients/mapped/Bacto_Soytone.yaml` and `data/ingredients/mapped/Sodium_L-lactate.yaml`. Both have **two** problems.

## 1. `mapping_status: REJECTED` but filed under `mapped/`

Both carry `mapping_status: REJECTED` while living in `data/ingredients/mapped/` and appearing in `data/curated/mapped_ingredients.yaml`. Either the rejection should move them to `unmapped/`, or the status is wrong.

## 2. The record `identifier` contradicts its own `ontology_mapping`

Per `docs/CURIE_STANDARD.md`, in MIM the record `identifier` **is** the ontology mapping CURIE for a mapped record. Neither of these satisfies that:

| file | `identifier` | `ontology_mapping.ontology_id` | problem |
|---|---|---|---|
| `Sodium_L-lactate.yaml` | `CHEBI:867561` | `CHEBI:232798` (sodium L-lactate) | identifier ≠ mapping; **and `867561` exceeds the `CHEBI: 300000` plausibility ceiling** in `conf/id_label_targets.yaml`, the signature of a foreign identifier wearing an OBO prefix |
| `Bacto_Soytone.yaml` | `CHEBI:8150` | `FOODON:03315720` ("vegetable protein, hydrolyzed") | identifier ≠ mapping, and the **prefixes disagree** — identifier says CHEBI, mapping says FOODON |

The `CHEBI:232798` and `FOODON:03315720` mappings both look correct; it is the `identifier` that is stale or wrong in each case.

## Why the plausibility gate did not catch `CHEBI:867561`

The id↔label gate validates `(ontology_id, ontology_label)` pairs. The bogus value is in the `identifier` field, which is not part of a validated pair — so an out-of-ceiling CHEBI can sit in the primary key indefinitely. Worth considering whether `identifier` should be range-checked too, given that in MIM it is by definition an ontology CURIE.

## Related

`Bacto_Soytone`'s mapping target `FOODON:03315720` is the same term already carried by `Phytone` and `Soya_Pepton` (see the duplicate-primary-key item in `NEXT_TASKS.md`), so resolving this should be coordinated with that dedup.

items.title: Canonical ingredient CURIE for cross-repo citation (CommunityMech ENVO linking)
items.body:
## Summary

CommunityMech is building ENVO-based cross-repo linking (its issue
[#30](https://github.com/CultureBotAI/CommunityMech/issues/30)). The **media**
half now works — a community's `environment_term` is matched against CultureMech
`source_environment`, emitting `related_media` blocks keyed on a shared ENVO term
(CommunityMech PR #211). The **ingredient** half is blocked on one MIM-side
question: **what is the stable canonical ingredient CURIE that an external repo
should cite?**

This issue asks MIM to confirm that, and to confirm the durability of the ENVO
`environmental_context` field (added in #1) as the join key.

## What CommunityMech found looking at MIM

- MIM's canonical ingredient identity is **`MIM:<Ingredient_Name>`** — 2200
  subjects in `mappings/ingredient_mappings.sssom.tsv`, with the `MIM:` prefix
  expanding to `.../data/ingredients/mapped/`, mapped to ontology terms
  (CHEBI/FOODON/…) via SSSOM. This matches `MAPPING_SEMANTICS.md` (the
  registry/identity-row pattern).
- Ingredient records under `data/ingredients/mapped/` carry
  `identifier: kgmicrobe.ingredient:…` / `CHEBI:…` and, where curated,
  `environmental_context[].environment_term` (ENVO). ~44 currently carry an
  ENVO context.
- The **`MediaIngredientMech:NNNNNN`** style id appears only in two `analysis/`
  reports (`merge_pattern_analysis.yaml`, `duplicates_and_variants.yaml`) and in
  **zero** canonical records or the unified mapping TSV.

The problem: **CommunityMech's schema references the last one.**
`RelatedIngredient.mediaingredientmech_id` has pattern `^MediaIngredientMech:\d{6}$`
— a scheme MIM does not use canonically — so there is no valid id for
CommunityMech to emit, and its 222 existing `related_ingredients` populate no id
at all.

## Asks (MIM-side confirmation, no code change strictly required)

1. **Canonical cross-repo id.** Confirm `MIM:<name>` is the stable identifier
   external repos should cite for an ingredient (as opposed to routing through the
   ingredient's `CHEBI:` mapping, or the legacy `MediaIngredientMech:NNNNNN`).
   If `MIM:<name>` labels are subject to renaming, is there a rename-stable
   surrogate?
2. **ENVO field durability + coverage.** Is `environmental_context` a maintained
   field going forward, and is broader population expected? Its coverage (~44
   ingredients) is what determines how much environment-based ingredient
   suggestion is possible downstream.
3. **CHEBI route.** For ingredients that `skos:exactMatch` a CHEBI term, is citing
   the `CHEBI:` id (which CommunityMech's `RelatedIngredient.chebi_term` already
   supports) an acceptable equivalent link? That would let CommunityMech link many
   ingredients today without waiting on id decisions.

## Downstream once confirmed

CommunityMech will align its schema (add `shared_environment_term` to
`RelatedIngredient`; correct the id field to match MIM's canonical scheme) and
extend its environment-based suggester to emit ingredient links. Tracked in
CommunityMech `NEXT_TASKS.md` §2c.

Context: CommunityMech PRs #210 (coverage dashboard) and #211 (media suggester).
